query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Implementing a closed‐loop, high-throughput catalyst discovery approach based on continuous-solvothermal synthesis at low temperatures and high alkalinity will promote controlled multimetal reduction and beneficial post-ageing Cu–Pt electronic coupling, thereby yielding automotive exhaust catalysts with improved activity and durability while lowering platinum-group-metal consumption.
generation.material_initial_state: Fresh 1 wt% multi-element alloy catalyst candidates prepared from up to 19 metal precursors and deposited on La-doped γ-Al2O3, typically containing agglomerates of fine metallic particles and not yet thermally aged.
generation.intervention: Use a closed-loop discovery campaign that employs automated continuous-solvothermal synthesis (200–350 °C, 20–35 MPa, with high alkalinity from 25 M NaOH) combined with post-ageing activity screening and Bayesian optimisation to select optimal compositions and processing conditions.
generation.conditions: Catalysts are exposed to accelerated thermal ageing (900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich, water-containing gas conditions) and then tested in a near-stoichiometric exhaust feed (containing 500 ppm NO, 5000 ppm CO, 200 ppm C3H6, 120 ppm i-C5H12, etc.) over the temperature range 100–500 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: The intervention fosters post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction—particularly the formation of electronically coupled Cu–Pt sites and controlled multimetal nucleation—which mediates the improved adsorption/activation dynamics and mitigates detrimental segregation or excessive Pt isolation.
generation.mechanism: High alkalinity and lowered synthesis temperatures support synchronous multimetal reduction and limit phase segregation. During ageing, the controlled electronic redistribution leads to beneficial Cu–Pt surface rearrangement that weakens overly strong CO binding, enhances redox buffering and oxygen mobility, and counters adverse Pt coordination (e.g., with Ni/Fe) that would otherwise hinder adsorption and catalytic activity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and catalysts discovered via random exploration, catalysts produced by the closed-loop method are expected to display at least a 5 °C lower T50 or a minimum 2 percentage-point improvement in conversion at 350 °C, along with overall enhanced low-temperature and total conversion post-ageing.
generation.baseline: The performance of typical Pd/Al2O3 catalysts tested under identical post-ageing conditions and conversion metrics, as well as the hit rate from randomly selected catalyst compositions, serve as the baseline.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to the explored five- to nineteen-element, 1 wt% catalyst systems on La-doped γ-Al2O3 under the specified accelerated ageing protocol and near-stoichiometric simulated exhaust conditions; detailed nanoscale structure–performance correlations remain to be quantitatively established.
generation.uncertainty: While the predicted improvements are supported by the design rationale, the exact magnitude of performance gains and the complete causal link between nanoscale reconstruction and catalytic activity require further quantitative validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize catalyst candidates using the described closed-loop, high-throughput continuous-solvothermal approach and age them under the specified accelerated conditions. Perform light-off measurements for species-resolved NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12 conversion (focusing on T50 and conversion at 350 °C) and compare the performance statistically against both a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and catalysts from a random compositional screen.
measurements: Light-off metrics (T50 and conversion at 350 °C) from the aged catalysts
FT-IR spectroscopy of CO adsorption pre- and post-ageing to detect electronic coupling changes (e.g., indicative of Cu–Pt interactions)
HAADF-STEM/EDS analysis to verify particle morphology and multimetal distribution, especially confirming controlled elemental segregation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the catalysts synthesized via the closed-loop approach do not yield statistically significant improvements (i.e., less than a 5 °C decrease in T50 or under a 2 percentage-point conversion increase at 350 °C) relative to the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark, or if the expected Cu–Pt electronic coupling and controlled multimetal distribution are not observed, then the hypothesis will be rejected.
